verdict.reasoning: The patient reports numbness in the left arm with tingling and difficulty playing the piano, indicating decreased dexterity. Transcript: 'I can't quite move my left arm... it's numb, and then I also feel some, like tingling in my fingertips.'
The patient states the symptoms have been present for at least two weeks and have worsened. Transcript: 'It's probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks, and it's kind of gotten worse.'

The patient reports tingling and numbness in the second, third, and fourth fingers on the palmar side, extending from the elbow to the hand. Transcript: 'I can feel it both in my, uh, um, you know a little bit in my elbow, and then in my arm, as well as in my hand... it's my second, third, and fourth finger.'

The patient reports difficulty playing the piano due to weakness, not pain. Transcript: 'I will say, um, well I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed it's been kind of harder to get the notes... No, no, it's not hurting, it's not hurting, it's, like, numb.'

The patient mentions feeling shoulder discomfort during boxing movements. Transcript: 'sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder. Like if I try to, if I try to like you know move like in boxing and stuff.'
The patient tried massage and warm baths without relief. Transcript: 'I tried massage, I tried some hot baths, and that didn't help with this numbness thing.'
The patient denies neck pain. Transcript: 'No, not, no, nothing.'
The patient denies leg weakness and reports normal gait. Transcript: 'Yeah, yeah, yeah, walking is normal, yeah.'
The patient denies seizures or loss of consciousness. Transcript: 'Ohh, no, no, no, no, nothing like that, mmm mmm.'

The patient had transient left eye peripheral vision loss lasting about 20 minutes. Transcript: 'I all of a sudden just couldn't see from the, uh, from my left eye... that just lasted maybe for, I don't know, twenty, twenty minutes?'
The patient had a bad cold or flu lasting about two weeks a month ago. Transcript: 'I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago... I was sick for probably good like two weeks.'
The patient reports feeling fatigued. Transcript: 'I just felt really, fatigued and I couldn't even get myself to the gym.'
The patient reports occasional tired headaches. Transcript: 'sometimes I get headaches but I think they're just tired headaches.'
The patient denies having chronic medical conditions. Transcript: 'in general, I'm, I'm pretty healthy. You know, I work out, uh, , and I, I don't really have any medical problems.'
The patient uses ibuprofen as needed. Transcript: 'I do take Ibuprofen because my muscles were sore.'
The patient takes vitamin D. Transcript: 'But, vitamin D I take.'
The patient takes iron with poor adherence. Transcript: 'my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but you know, they're just like huge pills so I, I, most of the time I just forget.'
The patient uses melatonin as needed. Transcript: 'And then, sometimes I take Melatonin to help me sleep.'
Allergies were not discussed in the transcript.

The patient's father has hypothyroidism and an autoimmune disease. Transcript: 'I know that my dad has I don't know if it it's hypo, I think it's hypothyroidism... he's got some autoimmune stuff going on.'

The patient's mother has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Transcript: 'my mom, she's actually not in a great shape. She's got diabetes type two... she's got hypertension... she's got high cholesterol.'
The patient takes boxing classes. Transcript: 'I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks.'
The patient had a recent single episode of heavy alcohol use. Transcript: 'I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me.'
The patient exercises regularly. Transcript: 'I work out.'
No vital signs were documented in the transcript.
No physical exam findings were documented in the transcript.
No diagnostic tests were performed during the consultation. Transcript: 'I think it's quite important that we do investigate it a bit further.'

The patient has left upper extremity paresthesia and weakness in digits 2 to 4 palmar for two weeks and worsening, with a pattern concerning for neurologic etiology. Transcript: 'I can't quite move my left arm... it's numb, and then I also feel some, like tingling in my fingertips.'
The distribution of symptoms raises consideration beyond a localized overuse injury. Transcript: 'I'm just wondering whether there's something a bit more than just the boxing here.'

Transient left visual field loss lasting about 20 minutes is considered a neuro-ophthalmic event requiring urgent evaluation. Transcript: 'you know, when you said you can't, your vision went, your peripheral vision was not there for about twenty.'
There is a recent viral illness and fatigue with temporal association noted. Transcript: 'I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago... I just felt really, fatigued.'

The patient has minor right hand knuckle pain from boxing and is using ibuprofen as needed. Transcript: 'I kind of hurt like my knuckles on my right hand. So that's been a little bit painful, so I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that.'
An urgent neurology referral was planned for further evaluation. Transcript: 'I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral.'
Neurologic workup is likely to include brain imaging as discussed. Transcript: 'What they, what that might entail is the brain scan and things like that.'

No steroids or disease-specific therapy will be started until a diagnosis is confirmed. Transcript: 'No, that's something we can't do. The treatment for it is actually some steroids and things like that, uh, when you have an acute you know, acute reaction or things like that. But, saying that, first we need to firm diagnosis.'

Patient was given emergency precautions for worsening weakness especially new leg involvement, severe headache, vomiting, seizures, or worsening or recurring visual symptoms. Transcript: 'if the weakness progresses to your legs, or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A and E.'

Patient is to continue current symptomatic measures such as ibuprofen as needed, and no new medications were initiated. Transcript: 'While you're waiting for this to be done... then that would be an A and E.'
